Parse an X.509 certificate

Source: R/x509.R
certprs.Rd

Reads the fields a verifier needs: who issued it, who it is for, when it is valid, what key it carries, and what that key is allowed to do. Use it to inspect the certificate of a timestamping authority or a signer before you decide to trust it, or as the first step of certchnvrf(). The DER decoder is the package's own; no system library or network is used.

Usage

certprs(cert)

Arguments

cert

The certificate, DER or PEM: a raw vector of DER bytes, or the path of a .der, .crt, .cer or .pem file.

Value

A list of class bricklayer_certificate with these elements:

  • version (integer) and serial (hex);

  • issuer and subject (distinguished names as text);

  • not_before and not_after (POSIXct, UTC);

  • signature_algorithm (a name such as "ECDSA-SHA256") and signature_oid;

  • signature and tbs (raw; the signed part);

  • key (a list: type "RSA" or "EC", bits, and the key values, with curve for EC);

  • is_ca and path_len;

  • key_usage and extended_key_usage (character; EKU as OIDs);

  • subject_rdns, issuer_rdns, san and name_constraints;

  • the policy fields policies, policy_mappings and require_explicit_policy;

  • the policy fields inhibit_policy_mapping and inhibit_any_policy;

  • self_signed (logical: issuer equals subject);

  • der (the bytes).

print() shows a summary.

Details

The certificate is decoded as DER (RFC 5280 section 4.1); a file whose text contains a -----BEGIN line is read as PEM and its base64 body decoded first (only the first certificate in the file is used). Version 1 certificates, without the explicit version field, are accepted. Extensions read: basic constraints, key usage, extended key usage, subject alternative name, name constraints, certificate policies, policy mappings and policy constraints, and inhibit any-policy. The signature is not checked here: that needs the issuer's key, which certchnvrf() supplies.

Errors: cert neither a raw vector nor the path of an existing file (a directory is refused); bytes that are not well-formed DER or carry trailing bytes; a DER structure that is not a certificate or has no signature.

See also

certchnvrf(), tsvrf().

Examples

# Pass the certificate file you were given (.der, .crt, .cer or .pem), for
# example the one a timestamping authority publishes, or raw DER bytes.
# Here: a small test chain shipped with the package, a self-signed P-256
# root and a leaf it issued (a throwaway test authority; trust it for
# nothing).
x509 <- function(f) {
  system.file("extdata", "x509", f, package = "rmoriebricklayer")
}
root <- certprs(x509("test-root.der"))
root
#> ╭── X.509 certificate ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
#> │   Subject             O=rmbl test, CN=EC256 Root                            │
#> │   Issuer              O=rmbl test, CN=EC256 Root                            │
#> │   Serial              52157dfd900c163c5027372ed4090b9d                      │
#> │   Valid from          2026-10-02 08:43:41                                   │
#> │   Valid to            2036-09-29 08:43:41                                   │
#> │   Key                 EC 256 bits                                           │
#> │   Signature           ECDSA-SHA256                                          │
#> │   Is a CA             TRUE                                                  │
#> │   Self-signed         TRUE                                                  │
#> │   Key usage           keyCertSign, cRLSign                                  │
#> │   Extended key usage  none stated                                           │
#> │                                                                             │
#> │   In force now, for 3,620 more days (until 2036-09-29).                     │
#> │   A self-signed CA certificate: a root, trusted or not, never verified.     │
#> │                                                                             │
#> │   What the certificate says about itself. Nothing here is checked:          │
#> │   certchnvrf() verifies it against trust anchors you choose.                │
#> ╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
leaf <- certprs(x509("test-leaf.der"))
leaf$subject
#> [1] "O=rmbl test, CN=EC256 Leaf"
leaf$key$curve
#> [1] "P-256"
c(leaf$not_before, leaf$not_after)
#> [1] "2026-10-02 08:43:41 UTC" "2031-10-01 08:43:41 UTC"

# the same root as PEM, the text form most authorities hand out
certprs(x509("test-root.pem"))$self_signed
#> [1] TRUE

# raw DER bytes work too
f <- x509("test-leaf.der")
der <- readBin(f, "raw", file.size(f))
identical(certprs(der)$serial, leaf$serial)
#> [1] TRUE

# bytes that are not a certificate
try(certprs(charToRaw("not a certificate")))
#> Error : not well-formed DER
